about.heading: About the Academic Union Network
about.text: The Academic Union Network (高校工会交流平台) is a volunteer network of master's students, doctoral students and postdoctoral researchers at universities across North America.
about.more: Its members are academic workers and union organizers on their own campuses. The network connects organizers across campuses and shares resources and organizing experience. It works to bring more international students, especially Chinese students, into union organizing alongside their domestic and immigrant colleagues.

purpose.heading: Why we made this page
purpose.introduction: This page brings together the pay and benefits that graduate workers' union contracts and university policies set, so that:
purpose.more: Graduate workers at dozens of US universities have formed unions and won contracts that set their pay, summer funding, tuition waivers and health insurance. The details are scattered across contract PDFs, university websites and news reports, so they are hard to find and harder to compare. Where no contract sets pay, the page uses the university's published funding policy, so that schools with and without union contracts can be compared.
reasons: Graduate workers can compare their pay and benefits with those at other schools, and see what other unions have won.
Organizers and bargaining committees can cite specific figures, with their sources, when preparing contract proposals.
Prospective graduate students can compare funding offers with what other schools provide, including summer pay and benefits.
Anyone can check our work: every figure links to its source document, with the passage quoted.
purpose.closing: We update the page when union members approve new contracts and schools publish new pay rates.

page.notice: Every figure links to its source. To report an error or suggest an improvement, please write to mail@academic-union-network.org.

sections.text: Most figures come from union contracts, published pay tables and university funding policies. A few come from university announcements, union summaries or news reports. Each figure links to its source passage, and to an archived copy where one exists. We record figures as the source states them. Some sources state pay per hour or per term, as a full-time rate, or per month without a set appointment length. For these, we calculate the yearly figure and mark it with an asterisk (*) in the chart and “calculated” in the table.

The page compares pay with two measures of the cost of living near campus. The first is rent: the Fair Market Rent that the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) publishes for a one-bedroom apartment in each campus's area. It includes utilities, and HUD sets it so that 40 percent of similar rentals in the area cost this much or less. HUD updates it each federal fiscal year, which begins in October. The page shows 12 months of this rent as a share of the year's pay. HUD considers renters who spend more than 30 percent of their income on rent cost-burdened. The second measure is living costs: the housing, food, transportation and personal expenses in the school's published cost of attendance for graduate students. The cost of attendance is the school's own figure for what a student needs. The page compares pay with these living costs month by month. Where a school pays for whole semesters over a different number of months than its cost of attendance covers, as Penn State does, the comparison is per semester instead.

Many unions cite the living wage from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Living Wage Calculator as a measure of what pay should cover. It is the hourly wage a full-time worker needs to pay for basic costs, including taxes, where they live. Each school's rent and living-cost details link to the calculator's page for the campus's county, for comparison with the school's pay. The page links to the calculator instead of showing its figures because its terms require a license to use figures for more than ten places.

Contracts and policies change, and documents can be unclear. Despite our checks, the data may contain errors. Minimum pay is the least a school may pay for an appointment, not what a typical student receives. Appointment lengths and weekly hours differ between schools, so read a figure's details before comparing it with another. Rankings compare minimum pay in dollars, not standards of living. Rents and prices differ widely between cities, and schools differ in many ways besides whether their graduate workers have a union contract.

This page and its data are for general information only, not legal, financial or employment advice. The data is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. Where these figures differ from an official contract or policy, the official document takes priority.

To report a mistake, or a newer contract or rate, email mail@academic-union-network.org with the school, the figure and a link to the source. We will check the source and correct the data where needed. We would also like to hear which schools or contracts to add, which comparisons or features would help, and how to improve this page.

about.heading: 关于高校工会交流平台
about.text: 高校工会交流平台（Academic Union Network）是一个志愿者网络，由北美各高校的硕士研究生、博士研究生和博士后组成。
about.more: 成员既是学术工作者，也是各自学校的工会组织者。平台联结各校的组织者，分享资源和组织经验。平台还致力于让更多国际学生，特别是中国留学生，与美国本地和移民同事一道参与工会组织工作。

purpose.heading: 我们为什么制作本页面
purpose.introduction: 本页面汇集研究生工人的工会合同（union contract）和校方政策规定的工资与福利，以便：
purpose.more: 美国数十所大学的研究生工人已经成立工会并赢得合同，合同规定了其工资、暑期资助（summer funding）、学费减免（tuition waiver）和医疗保险（health insurance）。相关细节分散在合同PDF、大学网站和新闻报道中，查找不易，比较更难。在没有合同规定工资的学校，本页面改用校方公布的资助政策，以便比较有无工会合同的学校。
reasons: 研究生工人可以将自己的工资和福利与其他学校比较，并了解其他工会争取到了什么。
组织者和谈判委员会在准备合同提案时，可以引用附有来源的具体数字。
研究生申请者可以将收到的资助方案与其他学校提供的条件（包括暑期工资和福利）比较。
任何人都可以核对我们的数据：每个数字都链接到其来源文件，并引用原文段落。
purpose.closing: 每当工会会员批准新合同、学校公布新的工资标准时，我们都会更新本页面。

zh.notice: 每个数字都链接到其来源。如需报告错误或提出改进建议，请通过邮箱（mail@academic-union-network.org）联系我们。

sections.text: 大多数数字来自工会合同（union contract）、公布的工资表和校方资助政策。少数来自校方公告、工会摘要或新闻报道。每个数字都链接到其原文段落；如有存档副本，也一并链接。我们按来源原文记录数字。有些来源按小时或按学期列出工资，或以全职标准列出，或按月列出但未规定雇佣期（appointment length）。我们据此折算出年度数字，在图表中以星号（*）标出，在表格中标注为“折算”。

本页面用两项指标衡量校园附近的生活开销，并与工资比较。第一项是租金，即美国住房和城市发展部（U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development，HUD）为各校区所在地区一居室公布的公平市场租金（Fair Market Rent）。这一租金包含水电等公用事业费；HUD设定时使该地区40%的同类出租房租金不超过这一水平。HUD每个联邦财政年度（从10月开始）更新一次。本页面显示12个月的这一租金占该学年工资的比例。HUD认为租金支出超过收入30%的租户属于住房成本负担过重（cost-burdened）。第二项是生活成本，即研究生就读费用（cost of attendance）中的住房、餐饮、交通和个人开支；就读费用是学校自己公布的学生所需费用。本页面按月比较工资和这些生活成本；如果学校按整学期发放工资，且发放月数与就读费用涵盖的月数不同（如Penn State），则改为按学期比较。

许多工会引用MIT生活工资计算器（MIT Living Wage Calculator）给出的生活工资（living wage），用以衡量工资应当足以支付哪些开支。生活工资是一名全职工作者在其居住地支付包括税费在内的基本开支所需的时薪。每所学校的租金和生活成本详情都链接到该计算器上校区所在县的页面，便于与该校工资比较。本页面只提供链接而不显示其数据，因为该计算器的使用条款规定，使用超过十个地点的数据须获得许可。

合同和政策会变化，文件也可能表述不清。尽管我们做了核对，数据仍可能有错误。最低工资（minimum pay）指学校依工会合同或公布的政策为一个TA/RA职位（appointment）支付的最低金额，不是法定最低工资，也不是一般学生实际获得的工资。各校的雇佣期和每周工时不同，因此比较数字之前，请先阅读其详情。排名比较的是以美元计的最低工资，而不是生活水平。各城市的租金和物价差异很大；除了研究生工人是否有工会合同之外，各校在许多方面也有差异。
本页面及其数据仅供一般参考，不构成法律、财务或就业建议。数据按“原样”提供，不附带任何形式的担保。如这些数字与正式合同或政策不符，以正式文件为准。
如果您发现错误，或发现更新的合同或工资标准，请通过邮箱（mail@academic-union-network.org）告诉我们，并注明学校、相关数字和来源链接。我们会对照来源核对，并在必要时更正数据。我们也希望了解应增加哪些学校或合同、哪些比较或功能会有帮助，以及本页面可以如何改进。

events.summary: Brown recognizes GLO as the exclusive bargaining representative of its Graduate Student Employees, as certified by the American Arbitration Association on December 6, 2018.
Bargaining for GLO's next contract began in February 2023; the union announced a first session between its bargaining committee and Brown's administration for Wednesday, February 15, 2023.

The previous (2020) agreement was due to expire on June 30, 2023; on June 28, Brown said the sides remained far apart and no successor or extension was expected by then, although bargaining had been under way since February.
In mid-November 2023 GLO and Brown reached agreement on stipends and on discrimination and harassment clauses, a breakthrough in talks that began in February.
GLO members voted electronically on whether to ratify the tentative agreement; voting opened December 11 and ran through midnight on Monday, December 18, 2023.

Bargaining for a successor contract began in February 2026. GLO opened with a 12% base stipend increase for FY27 (a $58,462 stipend), then 11% in FY28 and 10% in FY29; Brown countered with a 6.7% stipend increase over five years, which the union describes as a 0% raise in the first year.
Graduate fellows sought union recognition in March 2026 under a new Rhode Island law covering all graduate students; Brown declined to recognize them voluntarily on April 13, 2026.
The 2023 agreement expired at 11:59 pm on June 30, 2026, with bargaining for its successor still under way.

GLO grew out of Stand Up for Graduate Students (SUGS), formed in 2014 in response to a crisis in sixth-year funding for PhD students; in 2016 SUGS became Stand Up For Graduate Student Employees (SUGSE) and began organizing towards a labor union of graduate workers.

All Out for our first bargaining session 2-15-23!

The current 2020 agreement between Brown and the Graduate Labor Organization (GLO) expires on June 30, 2023, and we have been at the bargaining table since February seeking agreement on a new contract. Unfortunately, we remain very far apart on core issues, and there is no expectation that a successor agreement or an extension will be in place by the expiration date later this week.

The Graduate Labor Organization and the University reached an agreement on stipends and discrimination and harassment clauses in their new contract at a meeting last Wednesday — a major breakthrough in negotiations, which began in February.

Voting is live on the Tentative Agreement for our next contract! Now it’s up to all of us to vote to ratify this contract and make it official. Our ratification vote is open through midnight on Monday, December 18th.

When negotiations began in February, GLO proposed a 12% base stipend increase for fiscal year 2027, resulting in a stipend of $58,462. The union also proposed another 11% stipend increase in FY28 and a 10% increase in FY29.
The University countered GLO’s proposal by offering a 6.7% stipend increase over five years
They are currently proposing a 0% raise for next year along with raises in subsequent years that fall well below historical averages for inflation.
When is the contract expiring?
This Tuesday, June 30th at 11:59 pm.

On Wednesday, the three-year collective bargaining agreement between Brown and the Graduate Labor Organization expired. But according to University officials and GLO, there is no end in sight for a new contract.
Our Union was built upon the foundational work of Stand Up for Graduate Students (SUGS), which formed in 2014 and fought for rights and protections at Brown University.
In 2016, SUGS became Stand Up For Graduate Student Employees (SUGSE) and began organizing towards forming a labor union of graduate workers.

events.summary: On December 16, 2017 the National Labor Relations Board dismissed Columbia's objections to the December 2016 election and certified Graduate Workers of Columbia-UAW. The agreement recognizes the union as exclusive bargaining representative for wages, hours and working conditions of employees in the unit certified in Case No. 02-RC-143012.
The graduate-student workers first walked off their research, teaching and administrative jobs on March 15.
A 10-week strike by graduate instructors and others ended on January 7, 2022, the day after the two sides reached a tentative agreement.
Union members voted 97 percent in favor of ratifying the contract, according to a January 28 email from the provost.
Graduate student workers at Columbia began organizing a union in January 2014, and in the fall of 2014 Graduate Workers of Columbia (GWC-UAW) collected union cards from more than 1,700 of them.
In a National Labor Relations Board election held December 7 and 8, 2016 and counted December 9, the union won 1,602 votes to 623.

events.summary: A three-day strike in 2021 preceded the ratification of the 2021 agreement.
The 2021 agreement was ratified in 2021, following a three-day strike.
Bargaining for a successor to the 2021 agreement began in March 2025; by October 9, 2026 the parties had held 36 formal and six informal sessions without reaching a contract (Harvard's account).
HGSU-UAW members approved a strike authorization vote in late March 2026.
Strike from April 21 to June 1, 2026, which the union ended without a collective bargaining agreement.

Harvard's August 18, 2026 compensation proposal (not agreed): a single RA minimum for all disciplines, raised 6.07% on ratification to $51,972, then 2.5% on July 1, 2027 and 2028 and 2.75% on July 1, 2029 ($56,100 in FY30), with PhD Teaching Fellows raised to parity with RAs; hourly minimum $22.50 on ratification rising to $24.00 by July 1, 2029. Superseded by the University's October 2026 proposal.

Harvard's October 2026 compensation proposal (not agreed), dated October 8, 2026: as in August, a single RA minimum for all disciplines raised 6.07% on ratification to $51,972, but then 3% on each of July 1, 2027, 2028 and 2029 ($56,796 in FY30), with PhD Teaching Fellows raised to parity with RAs; the hourly minimum is unchanged from August, $22.50 on ratification rising to $24.00 by July 1, 2029.
HGSU-UAW members approved a second strike authorization vote in October 2026.

The graduate student unionization effort at Harvard became public in April 2015; organizers trace its roots to the Occupy Harvard movement of 2011. Later in 2015 the union voted to affiliate with the United Automobile Workers.

Harvard's first unionization election, in November 2016, did not produce a union majority: the revised tally was 1,396 for and 1,526 against. The National Labor Relations Board found the university's voter lists deficient and ordered a second election.
In the second election, held April 18 and 19, 2018, eligible student workers voted 1,931 to 1,523 to be represented by HGSU-UAW.
The National Labor Relations Board certified HGSU-UAW as the representative of Harvard's student workers on April 30, 2018, after neither side objected to the election.

events.summary: In a National Labor Relations Board election on April 4 and 5, 2022, MIT graduate workers voted 1,785 to 912 to be represented by UE.
The union kicked off negotiations for its first MIT contract with a rally on September 12, 2022.

Strike threat, not a strike: the union's account is that after it publicly announced a strike plan, and 24 hours before it was due to launch a public strike pledge, it won a tentative agreement on its first contract.
The union reports ratifying its first contract by Friday, September 22, 2023, ending a 12-month negotiation with MIT.
MIT and the union began bargaining a successor contract on April 24, 2026; five sessions had been held by June 4, 2026.

In late May 2026 MIT offered a 12-month contract extension with an immediate 3% raise for all union members; on June 1 the union declined it at the bargaining table without putting it to members (MIT's account) and proposed a 3-month extension, which MIT rejected.
MIT's letter reports that the 2023 agreement expired on May 31, 2026 and that most of its terms remain in effect until a new contract is signed.

On October 7, 2026 MIT and the union held a thirteenth negotiating session toward a new contract; the union presented a comprehensive proposal package and tentative agreements were reached on grievance procedure, nondiscrimination, workload and childcare. No successor agreement existed.

MIT graduate workers began meeting to discuss organizing a union in 2018; by late 2019 the organizing committee was looking at affiliating with a national union, and it announced its union drive publicly in September 2021.

events.summary: GSOC first won recognition in 2001, the first graduate union at a US private university.
A three-week strike, beginning Monday, April 26, 2021, after nearly a year of bargaining, preceded the 2020-2026 agreement.
Members ratified the agreement with a 99% yes vote on June 6, 2021.
GSOC moved from UAW Local 2110 to UAW Local 7902, which also represents NYU's contract faculty, after a membership-wide vote.
The agreement ran through August 31, 2026; either party could request successor negotiations from April 1, 2026.

Bargaining for a successor agreement was under way by the end of May 2026 (the June 1 update reports the second session). The October 7, 2026 update, after the 11th session, reports a tentative agreement on the Posting article and continuing talks on other articles.
The Graduate Student Organizing Committee was established in 1998.

Graduate employees voted 620 to 10 for GSOC-UAW and SET-UAW as their union in a December 2013 election certified by the American Arbitration Association, after NYU had stopped recognizing the union following the National Labor Relations Board's 2004 Brown University decision.
After the December 2013 election, NYU recognized GSOC-UAW again under its agreement with the union, and bargaining for a new contract began.

events.summary: Graduate students rejected unionization with Princeton Graduate Students United (PGSU), which intended to affiliate with UE, 652 to 391 (63% against), in an NLRB election held May 13 and 14, 2024. About half of graduate students were eligible: those titled "assistant in instruction" or "assistant in research", primarily in the natural sciences and engineering.

Graduate students began organizing Princeton Graduate Students United (PGSU) in 2016, after the National Labor Relations Board's ruling that year that graduate students at private universities may unionize. The drive paused after 2017, resumed with an affiliation with the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE) announced in February 2023, and lost its election in May 2024.

Graduate students enrolled in Purdue Online Learning or professional master’s programs are not eligible to hold graduate staff positions or receive tuition and fee remissions.
For graduate students employed in a Graduate Teaching Assistant, Graduate Lecturer or Graduate Research Assistant position, the value of a fee remission provided is not considered taxable income.

term_views.summary: Since the spring/summer 2023 term, Rackham Ph.D. students on the Ann Arbor campus in good academic standing and within the funding period of their offer of admission receive a spring/summer stipend at the level of their fall or winter stipend, making 12 months of stipend support. It treats Spring/Summer terms (Term III, IIIA, IIIB) only as possible employment periods paid at the same FTE rate; summer provisions cover only continuation of health benefits (Article XI, Section C; MOU II) and the summer ELI 994 training allowance for some international GSIs. term_views.label: Conditional
term_views.summary: Employees with a total employment fraction of .237 or more pay no tuition; at the lower fractions of .087, .137, and .187 they pay 56%, 46%, and 36% of assessed tuition (departments may set a lower share). An employee employed for less than the term in which they are enrolled gets no waiver. The university's HR page values the waiver at up to $14,443 per semester in-state and $28,888 out-of-state (undated; the amounts equal half of the 2024-25 graduate tuition and fees in the financial aid office's budget).

term_views.label: Guaranteed
term_views.summary: All employees appointed for a full employment period may enroll in GradCare, which the university's HR page describes as having no monthly premium for the employee. The University's contribution for employee-only coverage is 93% of the weighted average premium of the two lowest-cost comprehensive plans offered to all University employees, capped at the lesser of the total GradCare premium and the highest contribution given to regular non-bargained instructional staff; for dependents it pays 75% of the weighted average premium for children and 66% for a second adult.

events.summary: Negotiations on a successor to the 2023-2026 agreement began November 14, 2025, with a mediator from the Michigan Employment Relations Commission that the university had requested.

Graduate Student Research Assistants voted to join the GEO bargaining unit in an election run by the Michigan Employment Relations Commission, 299 to 25 (six spoiled ballots), with 17% of the 1,910 eligible voters casting ballots.
The 2023-2026 agreement reached its May 1, 2026 end date without a successor; under Article XXVI it continues in force unless either party gives 30 days' notice of termination.

Citing slow progress, the university asked the Michigan Employment Relations Commission to begin fact-finding; by September 18, 2026 the university had offered 2.5% a year over four years and GEO 9% a year (or CPI, if higher) over three years.
At the twenty-fourth negotiation session, GEO rejected the comprehensive package the university had proposed on September 18, 2026, and continued to present individual proposals.
GEO dates its founding to 1970, when teaching fellows first organized, as the University Teaching Fellows' Union, and petitioned the Michigan Employment Relations Commission for an election.
The Michigan Employment Relations Commission certified GEO as bargaining agent on April 15, 1974, after a certification election GEO won 807 to 424.

Effective August 28, 2023, the minimum FTE salary rate for four (4) calendar months GSIs and GSSAs on the Ann Arbor Campus will be $25,980 per term.

Under the new model, eligible students will receive a spring/summer stipend at the same level as the fall and winter terms, beginning with the 2023 spring/summer term.
Beginning in AY 2023–24, all funding packages in Ph.D. admissions offers will provide a spring/summer stipend at a level equivalent to the stipend offered in fall or winter terms.
Ph.D. students on the Ann Arbor campus who are in good academic standing and within the period of their offer letter of admission, including international students, are eligible for this new funding.

Exception: Through June 2026, students who are in their final spring/summer following the last academic year covered in their offer letter are eligible to receive this allocation if they are still currently enrolled and actively pursuing a degree.
Students who have exceeded the period of support described in their offer letter funding package will not be guaranteed to receive a spring/summer stipend via this funding change.

To the extent that students receive external funding (internships, employment, fellowships) equivalent or exceeding the established stipend, they should not receive additional funding through this new allocation.

Programs will provide the extended support to their students using available fellowship, GSRA, and GSI sources, allocated by equitable methods that each program will decide based on the academic needs of the program and the availability of sources.

The Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO) is the labor union representing Graduate Student Instructors (GSIs), Graduate Student Staff Assistants (GSSAs), and Graduate Student Research Assistants (GSRAs) at the University of Michigan.
GEO is Local 3550 of the American Federation of Teachers (AFT).
Formal negotiations between the university and the Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO) are scheduled to begin next week on November 14, 2025 in accordance with the current contract.
U-M’s and GEO’s negotiations teams held their first bargaining session today with the assistance of a mediator from the Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC).
the university has requested the assistance of a mediator appointed by the Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC) to facilitate the negotiations
The Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC) conducted the election for Graduate Student Research Assistants (GRSAs) to join GEO, which concluded on March 26.
MERC sent 1,910 ballots to GSRAs. Seventeen percent of eligible voters cast ballots, with 299 votes to join the union, 25 votes against joining, and six spoiled ballots.
Six scheduled negotiations remain before the current collective bargaining agreement expires on May 1, 2026.
In the event that a successor Agreement is not negotiated by 11:59 p.m. May 1, 2026, this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect
the university asked the Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC) to engage the parties in the fact-finding process.
Provides a 10% salary increase over a four-year contract (2.5% each year)
GEO currently proposes minimum salary increases of 27% over a three-year contract, 9% annually or an amount tied to the Consumer Price Index, whichever percentage is greater.
GEO was founded in 1970 and we won our first contract in 1975, making GEO the oldest continually running graduate employee union in the United States.

“Teaching Fellows” (TFs, as they were then called) first began to organize in 1970, when the University Teaching Fellows’ Union (TFU) collected enough signatures to warrant an election by the Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC).
They joined Research and Staff Assistants to form the Graduate Employees Organization (GEO)
This time the Administration agreed to an immediate MERC certification election. GEO was officially certified on April 15, 1974 after an overwhelming vote of 807 in favor, 424 against.

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: UAW 4811 dates its formation to 1999, when academic student employees at UC voted for UAW representation; the graduate local was then UAW 2865, which later merged with the postdocs' UAW 5810 to become UAW 4811.

Teaching assistants, readers and tutors voted for UAW representation in campus elections run by the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) in spring 1999: UCLA in March, Berkeley on May 13 (833 for, 293 against), and the remaining six campuses by June.
The first collective bargaining agreement between UC and the UAW for academic student employees took effect on June 1, 2000, after a long organizing campaign; it expired October 1, 2003.
UC recognized the UAW as the representative of Graduate Student Researchers in a Recognition Agreement dated December 8, 2021, after PERB certified the unit.
UC and UAW 4811 agreed to extend the 2022 BX and BR contracts to January 1, 2026, with a 4% increase on October 1, 2025, and to begin successor negotiations by July 7, 2025.
The extended 2022 BX and BR contracts expired on January 1, 2026, before a successor was reached.

UAW 4811 members passed an unfair-labor-practice strike authorization vote on February 13, 2026, with more than 93.3% of voters in favor. The union called off the strike when tentative agreements were reached in March.

After four weeks of confidential mediation, UC reached tentative agreements with UAW 4811 on Friday, March 13, 2026, for the unified ASE and GSR unit (and two staff units). The UC System Provost's letter of March 17, 2026 announced them to faculty.

UAW 4811 members ratified the agreement in a vote open from March 17 to March 20, 2026. In the ASE and GSR unit, 14,251 of 15,976 voters (89.2%) voted yes; across the three units voting together, 19,359 of 21,161 (91.5%).

events.summary: Graduate students at UW began organizing the union, then the Graduate Student Employee Action Coalition (GSEAC), in winter 1998; a year later its members voted to affiliate with the United Auto Workers.
After UW refused to bargain, saying state law prohibited it, the union struck for two weeks in June 2001, disrupting end-of-quarter grading.

A state law (Chapter 34, Laws of 2002, RCW 41.56.203) extended collective bargaining rights to UW's academic student employees, taking effect when the Governor signed it on March 14, 2002; GSEAC/UAW then petitioned the Public Employment Relations Commission for certification.

In a mail-ballot representation election run by the Public Employment Relations Commission, 1,391 voted for GSEAC/UAW and 979 for no representation, of about 4,569 eligible; the tally issued March 18, 2004.
UAW Local 4121 members ratified their first collective bargaining agreement with UW in 2004.
UW and UAW Local 4121 reached a tentative agreement on the successor contract after mediated sessions with a Public Employment Relations Commission mediator.
Members ratified the 2024-2027 agreement; UW announced it on May 23, 2024, and the contract took effect May 19, 2024, the ratification date under Article 39.

events.summary: Graduate and professional workers voted to form a union in early 2023, with 91 percent of the vote.
Local 33 members ratified the first contract 1,705 to 10 in a vote held December 15 and 16, 2023; Article 38 makes it effective on ratification, December 16.
The union was founded in 1990 as the Graduate Employees and Students Organization (GESO), which took the name Local 33 in 2016.

The National Labor Relations Board certified UNITE HERE Local 33 as the representative of Yale's graduate and professional student workers on January 18, 2023, after a tally issued January 9 counted 1,860 votes for the union and 179 against.
